title: Routed model context and compaction policy
summary: Each adapter reports the context window for an exact provider and model route; token measurement stays model-agnostic; compaction thresholds are resolved per route instead of from one global window.
firstReason: Per-route capacity is required as soon as one process talks to models of different sizes; keep it.

title: Durable image offload events
summary: When a request exceeds a route's image budget, a plugin records a durable image/offload event that names the oldest images to omit, then retries; the omission stays stable across later requests, route switches and compaction.
firstReason: Recording the omission keeps the model-visible image set reconstructable from the log; keep it.

title: Preset-scoped time context
summary: The plugin that injects the current time into the conversation is mounted only in presets that have the schedule tools; the minimal preset gets none.
firstReason: A context injection belongs to the preset that consumes it; otherwise every step in every preset pays for a message that nothing uses. This is a composition rule, not a mechanism.

title: Progressive Office skills with ordinary shell execution
summary: Office guidance is a compact router skill plus three format-specific authoring skills that the model loads by name, so ordinary editing does not pay for rendering instructions. Rendering uses a private, randomly named temporary directory in the workspace that is removed afterwards.
firstReason: Progressive loading is a prompt-budget decision, and the skills are data files. The note's mounting and shell-execution parts are superseded by later Office notes; one of them, 'Office skills in every deployment', is in this batch.

title: Shared agents root joins the user-global instruction chain
summary: User-global instructions are read from two ordered files: the harness home's `AGENTS.md`, then the shared `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` used by other agent tools. Identical content is rendered once, and both files are re-checked on resume so that an edit appears as a change notice.
firstReason: People who run several agent tools keep shared instructions in one place; copying them into the harness home creates two sources of truth. File locations and de-duplication are product behaviour.

title: Separate byte budgets for the user-global and project instruction chains
summary: User-global and project instruction files are rendered under separate byte budgets, so a large project chain can no longer push the user's global instructions out.
firstReason: With one shared budget the broadest files were dropped first, and those are the user's own. It is a prompt-assembly rule.

title: Office skills in every deployment with one Office Kit package
summary: Office skills are mounted in every deployment and read from one package's asset directory. One Office Kit package owns locating LibreOffice Kit, and a deployment without it lacks the capability instead of failing to load.
firstReason: Three separate lookups, and a load failure when the kit was absent, are removed. Inference: in Go the skill files are embedded in the binary, and the absent-dependency rule (degrade, do not fail start-up) applies to every optional external tool.

title: Process-specific checkout path and Web URL move to runtime context
summary: Two process-specific values, the implementation checkout path and the Web URL, move out of the system prompt into runtime context. The system prompt keeps only value-free guidance, so a different port or checkout no longer changes the prompt and misses the provider's prefix cache.
firstReason: Keeping the system prompt byte-stable across launches is a cost rule that holds for any host. The Go design should adopt the general rule (no per-process value in the system prompt); it has no earlier-format sessions to project.

title: Recallable compaction — index checkpoints, a state checkpoint, and in-session history recall
summary: Proposal, not built upstream: split compaction output into frozen index checkpoints that are never rewritten and one mutable state checkpoint, and give the model `history_read` and `history_search` tools to read compacted spans back from the session log.
firstReason: Adopt as later-priority scope. It needs only what the event-sourced log already provides, keeps the request prefix cache-stable across compactions and makes compaction recoverable for the model; it is not required for a first working compaction.

title: Read instruction files only through a filesystem provider
summary: Proposal: instruction files (such as `AGENTS.md`) are found and read only through the filesystem provider; the second code path that reads the local disk directly, used only by tests, is removed.
firstReason: Adopt: one read path through the filesystem interface means instruction discovery works the same for local, sandboxed and SSH workspaces, and needs one set of error and cancellation tests.

title: Prune unused skill registry API
summary: Rejected proposal: remove the method that lets a plugin register a skill directly at run time, because no shipped code calls it. Upstream keeps it as an intended extension path for third-party plugins.
firstReason: The reason for the rejection still holds: a plugin must be able to contribute a skill while the host runs. The mechanism changes, because a third-party plugin is a separate process (DH-ADR-4); run-time skill registration has to be a call in the plugin protocol rather than a method on an in-process service.

title: Fold the single compaction backend into its service package
summary: Rejected proposal: merge the compaction contract and its only complete backend into one package. Upstream keeps them apart because more compaction backends are planned.
firstReason: The rejection still holds in Go and costs less there: a small interface for compaction with the basic strategy as one implementation is ordinary Go, and the upstream tree already contains further compaction packages (image offload, tool-result pruning) beside the basic one.
